name: Truc
summary: 2-player 15th-century bluffing trick-taking game where raises can make opponents fold like poker.
rules_text: Play with a 32-card Piquet pack ranking 7 8 A K Q J 10 9 (suit irrelevant). First to 12 points wins a game. Each round both get 3 cards one at a time. Non-dealer may propose a redeal; if dealer agrees hands are discarded and redealt once only. Non-dealer leads, winner of trick leads next. Higher rank wins; equal ranks spoil the trick and it belongs to no one, leader repeats. Spoilt tricks count for the winner of the first trick when judging who won 2 tricks. Winning 2 of 3 tricks, or the first if 1-1 with one spoilt, wins the round for 1 point. Before leading, a player may raise by asking "Two more?". First raise makes round worth 2, then 4, 6, etc. Follower may accept and continue, or fold conceding the prior value. A player may concede any time. Declaring "Mon reste" raises the round to enough to win the game to 12; if accepted, winner of round wins game.
rating_reason: Bluff trick-taking likened to poker, strong hidden info.
